answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a stake that is slashed when it makes provably false claims, while rewards accrue only after independent peers validate useful work. Creating thousands of aliases then multiplies the capital locked up and the risk of forfeiture, but does not multiply influence: votes and payouts are weighted by stake at risk, not account count. Like water entering a glacier-fed karst or shifting dune, trust follows costly, verifiable commitments rather than names.
